reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program (Montana; focus year 2021)
    Question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for endangering property,
    including situations creating a reasonable potential for damage, or
    a pet capable of causing damage to persons or property?
*/

/* -----------------------
   Metadata (scenario setup)
   ----------------------- */
state(montana).
focus_year(2021).

/* -----------------------
   Scenario facts (encode the question's factual statement)
   ----------------------- */

landlord(landlord1).
tenant(tenant1).
rental_agreement(lease1).
premises(unit1).

/* Tenant has a pet capable of causing damage to persons or property. */
pet(dog1).
pet_capable_of_causing_damage(dog1, persons).
pet_capable_of_causing_damage(dog1, property).

/* Tenant knowingly allows the pet/activity on the premises, creating a reasonable potential of damage/injury. */
activity(keeping_dangerous_pet).
activity_on_premises(keeping_dangerous_pet, unit1).
tenant_knows_of_risk(tenant1, keeping_dangerous_pet).
tenant_allows_activity_on_premises(tenant1, keeping_dangerous_pet, unit1).

/* The activity creates a "reasonable potential" for premises damage or neighboring-tenant injury. */
activity_creates_reasonable_potential_premises_damage(keeping_dangerous_pet).
activity_creates_reasonable_potential_neighbor_injury(keeping_dangerous_pet).

/* Landlord serves a 3-day written notice specifying the 70-24-321(3) violation and terminates. */
landlord_delivered_written_notice(landlord1, tenant1, notice_days(3), violation_70_24_321_3).
landlord_elects_to_terminate(landlord1, tenant1, lease1).

/* Tenant does not vacate (holdover) and landlord does not consent to continued occupancy. */
tenant_remains_in_possession_without_consent(tenant1, unit1).

/* Helper predicate: succeeds when the encoded scenario is satisfied. */
scenario_statement :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    premises(Unit),
    tenant_allows_activity_on_premises(Tenant, keeping_dangerous_pet, Unit),
    tenant_knows_of_risk(Tenant, keeping_dangerous_pet),
    ( activity_creates_reasonable_potential_premises_damage(keeping_dangerous_pet)
    ; activity_creates_reasonable_potential_neighbor_injury(keeping_dangerous_pet)
    ),
    landlord_delivered_written_notice(_, Tenant, notice_days(3), violation_70_24_321_3),
    landlord_elects_to_terminate(_, Tenant, _),
    tenant_remains_in_possession_without_consent(Tenant, Unit).

/* -----------------------
   Statute translations
   ----------------------- */

/* MT Code  70-24-321(2) (2021): Tenant may not destroy/deface/damage/impair/remove any part of premises. */
statute_70_24_321_2_violation(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    tenant_destroys_or_damages_premises(Tenant).

/* MT Code  70-24-321(3) (2021): Tenant may not engage/knowingly allow activity that creates a reasonable
   potential that premises may be damaged/destroyed OR neighboring tenants may be injured. */
statute_70_24_321_3_violation(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    premises(Unit),
    tenant_allows_activity_on_premises(Tenant, Activity, Unit),
    tenant_knows_of_risk(Tenant, Activity),
    ( activity_creates_reasonable_potential_premises_damage(Activity)
    ; activity_creates_reasonable_potential_neighbor_injury(Activity)
    ).

/* MT Code  70-24-422(3) (2021): If violation of 70-24-321(2), landlord may terminate upon 3 days' written notice. */
statute_70_24_422_3_landlord_may_terminate(Tenant, notice_days(3)) :-
    statute_70_24_321_2_violation(Tenant).

/* MT Code  70-24-422(4) (2021): If violation of 70-24-321(3), landlord may terminate upon 3 days' written notice. */
statute_70_24_422_4_landlord_may_terminate(Tenant, notice_days(3)) :-
    statute_70_24_321_3_violation(Tenant).

/* MT Code  70-24-422(1) (2021): General noncompliance notice periods (only the parts relevant here).
   Included for completeness around the question's mention of pets.
   - Unauthorized pet: 3 days (422(1)(b)).
*/
statute_70_24_422_1_min_notice_days(unauthorized_pet, 3).

/* -----------------------
   Notice/termination mechanics (derived structure for reasoning)
   ----------------------- */

/* For these statutes, the minimum notice for the specific termination ground. */
legal_min_notice_days_for_ground(violation_70_24_321_2, 3).
legal_min_notice_days_for_ground(violation_70_24_321_3, 3).
legal_min_notice_days_for_ground(unauthorized_pet, 3).

/* A notice is legally sufficient if it is written, specifies the ground, and provides at least the minimum days. */
legal_notice_sufficient(Landlord, Tenant, Ground) :-
    landlord(Landlord),
    tenant(Tenant),
    landlord_delivered_written_notice(Landlord, Tenant, notice_days(DaysGiven), Ground),
    legal_min_notice_days_for_ground(Ground, MinDays),
    DaysGiven >= MinDays.

/* Landlord has statutory right to terminate (grounds). */
legal_landlord_has_termination_ground(Tenant, violation_70_24_321_2) :-
    statute_70_24_422_3_landlord_may_terminate(Tenant, notice_days(3)).
legal_landlord_has_termination_ground(Tenant, violation_70_24_321_3) :-
    statute_70_24_422_4_landlord_may_terminate(Tenant, notice_days(3)).

/* Termination becomes available when landlord has a ground + sufficient notice + landlord elects to terminate. */
legal_termination_available(Landlord, Tenant, Lease, Ground) :-
    rental_agreement(Lease),
    legal_landlord_has_termination_ground(Tenant, Ground),
    legal_notice_sufficient(Landlord, Tenant, Ground),
    landlord_elects_to_terminate(Landlord, Tenant, Lease).

/* MT Code  70-24-429(1) (2021): If tenant remains in possession without landlord consent after termination,
   landlord may bring an action for possession. */
statute_70_24_429_action_for_possession_available(Landlord, Tenant, Unit) :-
    landlord(Landlord),
    tenant(Tenant),
    premises(Unit),
    tenant_remains_in_possession_without_consent(Tenant, Unit).

/* Overall eviction (possession action) availability for this question's focus:
   If termination is available for endangering property (321(3)) or actual damage (321(2))
   and the tenant holds over without consent, the landlord can pursue eviction. */
legal_eviction_available(Landlord, Tenant, Lease, Unit) :-
    premises(Unit),
    ( legal_termination_available(Landlord, Tenant, Lease, violation_70_24_321_3)
    ; legal_termination_available(Landlord, Tenant, Lease, violation_70_24_321_2)
    ),
    statute_70_24_429_action_for_possession_available(Landlord, Tenant, Unit).

/* -----------------------
   Question answer
   ----------------------- */

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_eviction_available(landlord1, tenant1, lease1, unit1),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

/* -----------------------
   Main entrypoint (required)
   ----------------------- */
main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for endangering property? This includes where the law refers to situations that could result in damage to the property; or a pet capable of causing damage to persons or property.
